## Summary

Add an OSS-aligned **diff-coverage** signal on the Gerrit Verified lane (epic
`5664-b797-60b9-49ef` / soupy-bilineate-whiteeye, story S4): report line coverage on the lines a
change touches, reusing the coverage data the primary Ubuntu cell already collects. This is the
epic's chosen coverage improvement in place of raising the blunt global branch-coverage floor
(deferred in research 81fd because targeted mutation testing is the stronger oracle).

## Context / Problem

`_build-and-test.yml`'s default-suite step already collects in-process coverage on exactly one
cell (ubuntu-latest + py3.13) via `--cov=rebar --cov-report=term-missing:skip-covered`, but that
data is only rendered as a terminal report and a whole-tree `fail_under` floor
(`[tool.coverage.report]`, pyproject). Mainstream Python OSS additionally reports coverage on the
**changed lines** of each change, so a change that adds under-tested lines is visible even when
the global floor still passes. rebar had no such signal.

## Approach

Two edits, both on the coverage-bearing cell only, adding **no material hot-path latency** (the
epic's central constraint) because they reuse the coverage run that already happens:

1. **Emit `coverage.xml`.** Extend the existing conditional coverage-flag expression on the
   ubuntu+3.13 cell in the default-suite `pytest` step to also pass
   `--cov-report=xml:coverage.xml`. No new test run; pytest-cov writes the XML from the same
   session. The flags stay gated to `!startsWith(matrix.os, 'macos') && matrix.python-version ==
   '3.13'`, so no other cell changes.

2. **Add a report-only `diff-cover` step** after the default-suite step, guarded to the same
   ubuntu+3.13 predicate. It:
   - installs `diff-cover` ad hoc with `uv pip install` into the same `.venv` (a report tool,
     kept out of the lock — the exact pattern the pip-audit step uses);
   - selects the diff base per lane: on the Gerrit Verified lane the patchset's PARENT (`HEAD^`,
     deepened by one with `git fetch --deepen=1` like the pip-audit dependency-map gate, since a
     shallow patchset checkout has no parent object); on the push/branch lane `origin/main`;
   - runs `diff-cover coverage.xml --compare-branch="$base" --fail-under=0 --markdown-report
     "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"` — strictly **report-only** (`--fail-under=0` plus a `|| true` belt),
     writing the changed-line coverage into the job step summary;
   - guards on `coverage.xml` presence (skips with a `::notice::` if a patchset predates the
     step), and routes the refspec through an `env:` var (`GERRIT_REFSPEC`) rather than direct
     `${{ }}` interpolation into the run block, satisfying zizmor's template-injection audit.

**Non-blocking by design:** a diff-coverage dip is surfaced to the author, never a merge gate.
The enforcing coverage check remains the whole-tree `fail_under` floor. diff-cover is meaningful
only PRE-MERGE (on the post-merge push lane the change is already in origin/main, so the diff is
empty and diff-cover reports "no lines" — a harmless no-op). Because the Verified gate binds this
workflow from trusted main, the new step first executes against the NEXT change's patchset after
this one lands — that is the live-validation path.

## Parity contract

`tests/unit/test_ci_workflow_parity.py` pins the coverage-flag expression by exact string in two
places (the `_COVERAGE_FLAGS` constant + its regex, and the bash-lane expression renderer). Both
are updated to include `--cov-report=xml:coverage.xml`. The new diff-cover step is neither the
`default` nor the `integration` tier, so `test_matrix_keeps_every_test_tier_but_collects_coverage_once`
continues to pass unchanged.

## Latency

No measurable added Gerrit Verified hot-path latency: `coverage.xml` is a second reporter on the
already-running coverage session (milliseconds); the diff-cover step runs only on the single
ubuntu+3.13 cell, installs one small pure-python wheel, and diffs against an already-present
parent commit. It adds no new job and gates nothing.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The ubuntu+3.13 default-suite `pytest` invocation emits `coverage.xml` via
      `--cov-report=xml:coverage.xml`, with the flags still gated to that one cell.
- [ ] A report-only `diff-cover` step runs on ubuntu+3.13, computes a lane-correct diff base
      (`HEAD^` on the Gerrit lane, `origin/main` on the push lane), and never fails the job
      (`--fail-under=0`).
- [ ] The refspec is env-routed (no direct `${{ }}` interpolation in the run block); `make lint`
      (ruff + format + complexity baseline + zizmor over the vote path + actionlint) passes.
- [ ] `tests/unit/test_ci_workflow_parity.py` passes with the updated `_COVERAGE_FLAGS`.
- [ ] Adds no measurable Gerrit Verified hot-path latency (epic constraint).
